_comment: The MicroVM guest images this repo owns, and the memory tier each carries.
SCOPE. This AWS account is shared. It also holds managed-agents-runtime-*
and managed-agents-production-runtime (the serverless-agent runtime, built
from the blue repo), blue-* experiments, nslabs-benchmark-runtime, and
osb-tpl-* images built per customer template at run time by
internal/api/template_microvm_build.go. None of those are ours. Every name
here must start with ownedPrefix and release.sh refuses otherwise, so a
typo cannot reach another product's runtime.
TIERS. Memory is a property of the IMAGE, not of a launch: RunMicrovmInput
carries no memory field. A size tier IS an image, so N sizes means N images
built from ONE artifact. A tier built but not configured is refused at
create; a tier configured but not built fails at launch — so release.sh
prints the control-plane configuration that matches what it just published.
FRESHNESS. The published image drifted three weeks behind the guest code
once: /oc/secrets, /oc/envs and /oc/stats landed 2026-09-01 and nothing
rebuilt prod, so the control plane called routes its own guests did not
serve. An unregistered path falls through to the agent's gRPC listener,
which answers 415 with an empty body — invisible until the first customer
whose create carried a secret. One artifact, every tier, on every change.

DEFAULT TIER. The default image's memoryMB must equal awsvm's deliveredMicrovmMemoryMB (currently 4096). That constant is what metering prices on, so an image below it bills every default create for memory it did not get — which is exactly what happened: the lite images were published at 2048 while the constant was raised to 4096 on 2026-08-24, so prod metered 4096 on a 2048 box. manifest.py asserts the two agree on every run.
